verdict.rationale: Neon's neon.ts is a config-as-code file committed to the repo that declares services, including Functions, and is applied through inspect/plan/apply logic. That gives some versioning and a pre-apply review step for function/automation definitions. Snapshot and branch restore cover database data and schema, not automations, so they are not credited here. missing for 10: documented rollback of automations/functions, explicit automation version history, a documented review/approval workflow for automation changes, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: `neon.ts` is a TypeScript config file you commit to your repository. It declares which Neon services exist on your project and how each branch is configured
To call the same `inspect` / `plan` / `apply` logic from your own script or CI job instead of the CLI, see `@neon/config-runtime`.
Declare the AI Gateway and the function in `neon.ts`.
